prediction_text: Rupert will not get the honour of these wars; Essex will have the better of him and worst him. Rupert's significator the Sun is peregrine and in his detriment in a fixed sign, and is disposed of by Venus, Essex's significator, who is in reception with Saturn and casts an aspect to the cusp of the tenth; the Moon also casts her sinister aspect to the tenth cusp. Rupert's credit and command will decline under Essex's advantage rather than rise to lasting honour.
timing: No honour for Rupert in the present course of the war (the campaign following Edgehill, late 1642 into 1643); his disadvantage is fixed in character rather than a momentary reverse.
basis: Classical horary (Lilly): quesited as a person of eminency taken by the 10th house and its lord the Sun; Sun peregrine and in detriment in a fixed sign = weak dignity, no honour. Opponent Essex by Venus, lady of the opposite house, in reception with Saturn and disposing of the Sun: the opponent holds power over the quesited's significator. Venus dexter aspect to 10th cusp favours Essex's claim on honour; Moon sinister aspect to 10th cusp confirms Rupert's honour is afflicted.
